Differentiation potency of fetal and adult MSCs by single-cell entropy (SCENT)

Signalling entropy rate across osteogenic differentiation, each cohort normalised separately

Charles

24 August 2026

1 Background

This document computes the signalling entropy rate (SR) for the fetal (fMSC) and adult (aMSC) osteogenic differentiation time courses, following

Teschendorff AE, Enver T. Single-cell entropy for accurate estimation of differentiation potency from a cell’s transcriptome. Nat Commun 8:15599 (2017). doi:10.1038/ncomms15599

with the method as originally introduced in Banerji et al., Sci Rep 3:3039 (2013).

SR treats the transcriptome as a weighting of a protein-protein interaction (PPI) network and measures the promiscuity of signalling flux over that network. A random walk is defined on the PPI adjacency matrix \(A\) with the expression vector \(x\) as node weights,

\[p_{ij} = \frac{a_{ij}\,x_j}{s_i}, \qquad s_i = \sum_j a_{ij} x_j,\]

whose stationary distribution is \(\pi_i = x_i s_i / \sum_k x_k s_k\). With local entropies \(S_i = -\sum_j p_{ij}\log p_{ij}\), the global rate is normalised by the maximum entropy rate of the network, \(\log\lambda_{\max}(A)\):

\[\mathrm{SR} = \frac{\sum_i \pi_i S_i}{\log \lambda_{\max}(A)} \in [0,1].\]

High SR means signalling flux is spread broadly over the network — the signature of an undifferentiated, high-potency state. SR falls as cells commit.

Scope note. These are bulk RNA-seq libraries, not single cells. SR is well defined on bulk data (that is where the method originated), but a bulk value is a population average and cannot resolve potency heterogeneity between cells, which is the specific contribution of the 2017 paper. Interpret each value as the mean potency of the population in that well.

2 Cohorts are scored separately

The fetal and adult cohorts were sequenced in different batches, so cohort is confounded with batch. Both cohorts are therefore processed independently and in sequence in this one document: gene filtering, the variance-stabilising transform, and the PPI subnetwork are all derived within a cohort, and no cross-cohort normalisation is attempted.

The consequence is that the two sets of SR values are not on a common scale. Each cohort yields a different set of expressed genes, hence a different maximally connected subnetwork and a different normalising constant \(\log\lambda_{\max}\). Within-cohort contrasts — time, and OD versus CTRL — are unaffected and are the intended readout. The combined figure below uses free y-axes for that reason, and no fetal-versus-adult test is performed.

The net17Jan16 network shipped with SCENT (11,751 nodes, Entrez IDs, derived from Pathway Commons). A copy lives in the repository so this document is self-contained. SR values are only comparable within a fixed network and normalisation — the smaller net13Jun12 network from the 2017 paper puts the same samples near 0.916 rather than 0.966.

load(file.path(PROJECT, "data", "ppi", "net17Jan16.rda"))   # -> net17Jan16.m
net <- net17Jan16.m
cat(sprintf("PPI network: %d nodes, %d edges\n", nrow(net), sum(net) / 2))
## PPI network: 11751 nodes, 1504486 edges

5 Method implementation

DoIntegPPI intersects the expression matrix with the network and keeps the maximally connected component; CompSRana computes SR per sample. If the SCENT package is not installed, the fallback below implements the identical formulas. It uses the closed form (exact for a binary adjacency matrix)

\[S_i = \log s_i - \frac{\bigl(A\,(x \odot \log x)\bigr)_i}{s_i}\]

which avoids ever allocating the dense \(n \times n\) stochastic matrix.

integ_ppi <- function(exp.m, ppiA.m) {
  common <- intersect(rownames(ppiA.m), rownames(exp.m))
  stopifnot(length(common) >= 5000)
  adj <- ppiA.m[common, common]
  cl  <- igraph::components(igraph::graph_from_adjacency_matrix(
           adj, mode = "undirected"))
  mc  <- which(cl$membership == which.max(cl$csize))
  adj <- adj[mc, mc]
  list(expMC = exp.m[rownames(adj), ], adjMC = adj)
}

comp_max_sr <- function(adj.m) {
  fa <- function(x, extra = NULL) as.vector(adj.m %*% x)
  ap <- igraph::arpack(fa, options = list(n = nrow(adj.m), nev = 1, which = "LM"),
                       sym = TRUE)
  log(ap$values)
}

comp_sr <- function(integ.l) {
  A <- Matrix::Matrix(integ.l$adjMC, sparse = TRUE)
  maxSR <- comp_max_sr(integ.l$adjMC)
  sr <- apply(integ.l$expMC, 2, function(x) {
    s  <- as.vector(A %*% x)
    S  <- log(s) - as.vector(A %*% (x * log(x))) / s   # local entropies
    pi <- x * s; pi <- pi / sum(pi)                    # stationary distribution
    sum(pi * S) / maxSR
  })
  list(SR = sr, maxSR = maxSR)
}

score_cohort() runs the whole per-cohort pipeline: subset, gene filter (>= 10 counts in >= half that cohort’s libraries), blind DESeq2::vst, Ensembl to Entrez mapping (most highly expressed gene wins where several map to one Entrez ID), network integration, and SR.

score_cohort <- function(cohort) {
  message("=== ", cohort, " ===")
  smp <- coldata[coldata$cohort == cohort, ]
  smp <- smp[order(smp$Donor, as.integer(sub("D", "", smp$Time)), smp$Condition), ]
  cts <- counts_all[, rownames(smp)]
  smp$Donor <- factor(make.names(smp$Donor))     # DESeq2 dislikes spaces

  keep <- rowSums(cts >= 10) >= floor(0.5 * ncol(cts))
  message(sprintf("  %d libraries, %d donors, kept %d / %d genes",
                  ncol(cts), dplyr::n_distinct(smp$Donor), sum(keep), length(keep)))

  dds  <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(round(as.matrix(cts[keep, ])),
                                 colData = smp, design = ~ Donor)
  expr <- assay(vst(dds, blind = TRUE))
  stopifnot(min(expr) > 0)                       # SR needs strictly positive input

  ez   <- AnnotationDbi::mapIds(org.Hs.eg.db, keys = rownames(expr),
                                keytype = "ENSEMBL", column = "ENTREZID",
                                multiVals = "first")
  expr <- expr[!is.na(ez), ]; ez <- ez[!is.na(ez)]
  ord  <- order(rowMeans(expr), decreasing = TRUE)
  expr <- expr[ord, ]; ez <- ez[ord]
  dup  <- duplicated(ez)
  expr <- expr[!dup, ]; rownames(expr) <- ez[!dup]

  if (requireNamespace("SCENT", quietly = TRUE)) {
    integ <- SCENT::DoIntegPPI(exp.m = expr, ppiA.m = net)
    sr    <- SCENT::CompSRana(integ, local = FALSE, mc.cores = 1)$SR
    names(sr) <- colnames(integ$expMC)   # CompSRana returns an unnamed vector
    maxsr <- comp_max_sr(integ$adjMC)
  } else {
    integ <- integ_ppi(expr, net)
    res   <- comp_sr(integ)
    sr    <- res$SR; maxsr <- res$maxSR
  }

  smp$SR   <- as.numeric(sr[rownames(smp)])
  smp$day  <- as.integer(sub("D", "", smp$Time))
  smp$Time <- factor(smp$Time, levels = TORDER)
  message(sprintf("  subnetwork %d genes, maxSR = %.4f, SR %.5f - %.5f",
                  nrow(integ$adjMC), maxsr, min(smp$SR), max(smp$SR)))

  list(cohort = cohort, smp = smp, n_genes = nrow(integ$adjMC),
       n_edges = sum(integ$adjMC) / 2, maxSR = maxsr, n_kept = sum(keep))
}

Reporting helpers, so each cohort section is a single call.

# Reference values from the equivalent Python implementation on the same inputs.
EXPECTED <- list(
  fetal = list(genes = 8361, maxSR = 6.9282, mean = 0.96622, lo = 0.96518, hi = 0.96747),
  adult = list(genes = 8511, maxSR = 6.9309, mean = 0.96571, lo = 0.96480, hi = 0.96664)
)

check_tbl <- function(res) {
  e <- EXPECTED[[res$cohort]]
  knitr::kable(data.frame(
    quantity = c("genes in connected component", "maxSR", "mean SR", "min SR", "max SR"),
    expected = c(e$genes, e$maxSR, e$mean, e$lo, e$hi),
    observed = c(res$n_genes, res$maxSR, mean(res$smp$SR),
                 min(res$smp$SR), max(res$smp$SR))
  ), digits = 5,
  caption = sprintf("%s cohort: observed versus reference values", res$cohort))
}

plot_traj <- function(res) {
  ggplot(res$smp, aes(Time, SR, colour = Condition, group = Condition)) +
    stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "line", linewidth = 1.1) +
    stat_summary(fun.data = mean_se, geom = "pointrange", size = 0.6) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = PAL) +
    labs(x = "day", y = "signalling entropy rate (SR)", colour = NULL,
         title = sprintf("%s MSC potency across osteogenic differentiation",
                         res$cohort),
         subtitle = sprintf("%d libraries, %d donors, %d network genes",
                            nrow(res$smp), dplyr::n_distinct(res$smp$Donor),
                            res$n_genes)) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 13)
}

plot_donors <- function(res) {
  ggplot(res$smp, aes(day, SR, colour = Condition)) +
    geom_point(size = 1.8) + geom_line(aes(group = Condition), alpha = 0.7) +
    facet_wrap(~ Donor, nrow = 1) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = PAL) +
    labs(x = "day", y = "SR", colour = NULL) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 12)
}

stats_for <- function(res) {
  smp <- res$smp
  trend <- lapply(c("OD", "CTRL"), function(arm) {
    s  <- smp[smp$Condition %in% c(arm, "Base"), ]
    ct <- cor.test(s$day, s$SR, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)
    data.frame(cohort = res$cohort, test = paste("SR vs day,", arm, "arm"),
               n = nrow(s), statistic = unname(ct$estimate), p = ct$p.value)
  }) %>% bind_rows()

  w <- smp %>%
    filter(Condition %in% c("OD", "CTRL")) %>%
    select(Donor, Time, Condition, SR) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = Condition, values_from = SR) %>%
    tidyr::drop_na()
  wt <- wilcox.test(w$OD, w$CTRL, paired = TRUE)

  bind_rows(trend,
    data.frame(cohort = res$cohort, test = "OD vs CTRL (paired, donor x day)",
               n = nrow(w), statistic = unname(wt$statistic), p = wt$p.value))
}

6 Run both cohorts

Fetal first, then adult. Each pass is fully independent of the other.

fits <- lapply(COHORTS, score_cohort)
names(fits) <- COHORTS
plot_traj(fits$fetal)

8.1 Statistics

Within-cohort tests only: SR versus time in each arm (the D0 baseline is shared and enters both), and osteogenic induction versus control paired within donor and day.

stats_tbl <- bind_rows(lapply(fits, stats_for))
knitr::kable(stats_tbl, digits = c(0, 0, 0, 3, 8),
             caption = "Signalling entropy rate, within-cohort statistics")
Signalling entropy rate, within-cohort statistics

fetal OD vs CTRL (paired, donor x day) 24 105.000 0.20761657
adult SR vs day, OD arm 21 -0.786 0.00002367
adult SR vs day, CTRL arm 21 -0.841 0.00000175

write.csv(stats_tbl, file.path(OUTDIR, "scent_sr_stats_both_R.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

get_stat <- function(coh, pattern, what = "statistic")
  stats_tbl[stats_tbl$cohort == coh & grepl(pattern, stats_tbl$test), what][1]

Reference values from the Python run: fetal OD \(\rho = -0.82\) (\(p = 1.1\times10^{-7}\)), fetal CTRL \(\rho = -0.94\) (\(p = 8.1\times10^{-14}\)), OD versus CTRL \(p = 0.19\); adult OD \(\rho = -0.79\) (\(p = 2.4\times10^{-5}\)), adult CTRL \(\rho = -0.84\) (\(p = 1.8\times10^{-6}\)), OD versus CTRL \(p = 0.47\).

9 Interpretation

Both cohorts lose signalling entropy monotonically over the 17-day course — fetal \(\rho\) = -0.82 and adult \(\rho\) = -0.79 in the induced arm — consistent with a progressive loss of differentiation potency as the network concentrates flux onto fewer signalling routes.

The decline is, however, at least as steep in the non-induced control arm (fetal \(\rho\) = -0.94, adult \(\rho\) = -0.84), and osteogenic induction adds no detectable further drop once donor and day are matched (fetal \(p\) = 0.21, adult \(p\) = 0.50). On this dataset SR therefore tracks time in culture — confluence, contact inhibition, replicative age — rather than osteogenic commitment specifically. It should not be presented as a readout of the differentiation being induced without an experiment that separates culture duration from induction, for instance density-matched sampling or a second differentiation lineage as a comparator.

Because the cohorts are confounded with sequencing batch and are normalised separately here, the fetal and adult SR values describe within-cohort dynamics only and are not contrasted with each other.
